mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is a leading indicator of equity returns. A low federal funds rate (as measured by the current value) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced discount rates on equity cash flows. This relationship holds regardless of the absolute value of FEDFUNDS, as the series is always interpreted as a signal for positive returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in any instance where FEDFUNDS is observed, or the Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL value above 260 indicates high inflation, which triggers a monetary policy response and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 260, or the Rank IC between CPIAUCSL and 20-day returns is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 3.5% and the quarterly GDP (GDPC1) is above 19000 billion dollars, the economy is in a tight labor market with strong growth, which increases corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction condition (UNRATE < 3.5% AND GDPC1 > 19000) is met in more than 60% of instances where the 60-day forward returns are negative, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is negative in the tightening regime over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 3.0%) indicates a tight labor market, which is associated with strong economic growth and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE < 3.0%, or the Rank IC between UNRATE and 5-day returns is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is above 109.5 and housing starts (HOUST) are above 1360, the economy is experiencing strong supply and demand, which increases corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction condition (INDPRO > 109.5 AND HOUST > 1360) is met in more than 60% of instances where the 60-day forward returns are negative, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in any instance where GDPC1 is observed, or the Rank IC between GDPC1 and 60-day returns is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High housing starts (HOUST > 1400) indicate strong demand for residential construction, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion and positive corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances where HOUST > 1400, or the Rank IC between HOUST and 5-day returns is negative over any 3-year rolling window.
